project.summary: Forgewright is a local-first, provider-neutral engineering orchestration toolkit with an evidence-backed six-phase delivery pipeline and optional domain capability packs.

roots.purpose: Canonical boot, solve, verification, clarification, audit, and escalation contracts.
Senior specialist skills and shared pipeline protocols used by routed roles.
Canonical TypeScript MCP runtime, middleware, tools, and runtime tests.
Project initialization, onboarding, Docs Hub, and local operator commands.
Provider-neutral local CI, release, setup, synchronization, and runtime automation.
Machine-readable public and internal data contracts.
Product, architecture, roadmap, workflow, operations, and migration sources rendered by Docs Hub.
Repository-level deterministic unit, integration, contract, hook, and release verification.
Project-owned templates installed or synchronized into supported client workspaces.

backlog.title: Identify the active agent runtime and optimize subagent routing with current token prices
acceptance: Every request identifies the active execution surface, provider, capability source, and available concurrency before dispatch planning.
Every candidate subagent model is compared using current first-party input, cached-input, and output token pricing; missing or host-specific actual cost stays explicitly UNVERIFIED.
Routing prioritizes acceptance effectiveness, then wall-clock speed, total tokens, and estimated token cost; small coupled work records no-spawn.
A cheaper model is rejected when its retry, verification, or critical-path risk makes the overall plan less effective.

backlog.title: Wire the change-aware Docs Hub gate into precommit, full local CI, and required release checks
acceptance: Material code/config/runtime changes fail when the canonical state is absent from the same changeset.
Strict doctor and a fresh temporary HTML/CSS build pass without modifying source files.
Precommit and provider-neutral required checks invoke the same local gate.

backlog.title: Render structure, roadmap, flows, backlog, status, and freshness as accessible static HTML/CSS
acceptance: Every canonical project-state section is visible without JavaScript.
Each recorded project flow is shown as a Mermaid-derived static SVG with arrows, Mermaid source, and ordered-step fallback.
README exposes the continuous baseline, checkpoint, strict-gate, and final-build lifecycle plus the generated control-center paths.
Missing, empty, stale, blocked, and unknown states remain explicit.
The portal is usable at mobile and desktop widths without horizontal viewport overflow.

backlog.title: Reconcile historical status documents with the canonical project-state contract
acceptance: Historical task snapshots are clearly labeled or archived.
Current status readers are directed to docs/project-state.json and the generated portal.

backlog.title: Expand the strict approved catalog after resolving legacy link and anchor debt
acceptance: Every newly approved document passes strict link, anchor, diagram, privacy, and state-reference diagnostics.
The manifest allowlist expands without weakening fail-closed Docs Hub checks.

backlog.title: Keep behavioral test oracles locked to explicit current requirements
acceptance: A red test, green-suite goal, or current implementation cannot authorize weakening, deleting, skipping, regenerating, or rewriting behavioral expectations.
When expected behavior is missing, ambiguous, or contradictory, execution blocks and asks the user or product owner instead of inventing a test oracle.
Behavioral tests change only after an explicit current requirement or acceptance-criteria change; test infrastructure repairs must preserve the behavioral oracle and coverage.
Deterministic adversarial replay rejects test-oracle hacking and an empirical weak-model run preserves the test while reporting REQUIREMENT_BLOCKED.

backlog.title: Close legacy evidence, traceability, payment routing, RED-GREEN, signed-review, and dirty-tree bypasses
acceptance: Schema v1 and trivial or unrelated verifier evidence cannot complete code changes.
Every acceptance ID maps to exact concrete invoked test references and the machine-derived execution manifest matches the command.
Every negative_paths entry has an exact negative_path_bindings record with an ID, acceptance IDs, and invoked refs.
Every final-tree verifier is replayed from its exact stored argv; a nonzero, missing, timed-out, or worktree-mutating command blocks completion.
Payment, billing, IAP, receipt, entitlement, subscription, and checkout work is always HARD/DEEP and requires contract, runtime, E2E, and signed review-2 evidence.
Fixes require the same verifier RED to GREEN chain; HARD fixes also require pre-mutation GREEN, mutation failure, and exact final GREEN with tree restoration.

Only OpenSSH Ed25519 review-2 signatures trusted by external FORGEWRIGHT_REVIEW_ALLOWED_SIGNERS or ~/.forgewright/reviewers.allowed_signers can approve HARD work; review-1/self-authored JSON is UNVERIFIED.
Any staged, unstaged, tracked, or untracked nonignored source change invalidates prior evidence; secrets and private keys stay outside the workspace.

Verifier-owned evidence and volatile runtime memory, session, telemetry, cache, and review-handoff state cannot invalidate evidence merely by operating; arbitrary ignored project content remains fingerprinted.
An opaque platform-native Codex turn_id cannot shadow current evidence; selection is frozen once, while mapped-but-invalid selectors and non-correlated responses block.
Evidence and linked review reads are bounded regular-file operations that reject symlinks, path escape, and schema-v2 turn-to-filename mismatches.

status.summary: README now presents the Continuous Project Control Center as a primary capability, including the Mermaid pipeline, runtime/token-aware dispatch order, exact generated-site paths, and baseline/checkpoint/gate/final-build lifecycle. Every request identifies its active execution runtime before dispatch planning; candidate subagent models use current official token prices as cost evidence, while routing prioritizes effectiveness, wall-clock speed, total tokens, then estimated token cost. Small coupled work records no-spawn. Provider-native lifecycle hooks now inject a bounded inventory for every active canonical kernel rule across Codex, Claude, Gemini, Antigravity, and Cursor; project adapters resolve the Git root, while global installs use the trusted absolute framework runtime to validate and read the current project's manifest without executing project-supplied hook code. The off kill switch remains available. Rule-context failures are fail-open and do not replace existing Stop or security gates. Static validation now locks the exact six-rule ID-to-source inventory, while installer and doctor migrations recognize only exact trusted Forgewright-owned commands and preserve similarly named user hooks. The Stop lifecycle adds a read-only Docs continuity check that defaults to observe, derives custom JSON/YAML/asset sources from the current manifest, rejects unsafe catalog paths, binds cached fingerprints to current manifest semantics, and permits at most one stale-receipt refresh request in enforce mode before allowing UNVERIFIED. Docs Hub flow pages render every canonical ordered flow as a Mermaid-derived static SVG with visible arrows, Mermaid source, and accessible ordered-step fallback. Every material project update resolves the continuous Docs Hub contract; missing, legacy, or proportional projects are non-destructively initialized or migrated first. Documentation writes still use a pre-write governance gate that defaults to updating canonical truth and rejects duplicate, out-of-scope, transient, generated-source, or unresolved stale-truth artifacts. Requirement-locked test-oracle enforcement remains active across the delivery pipeline. H0 and the H1 HarnessAdapter compatibility contract are complete locally, with bounded Stop re-entry/single replay, exact MCP ownership leases, and project/session continuity integrated as safety controls; these controls do not complete the still-planned H2 TrajectoryLedger, H3 containment, H4 full replay, H5 live provider evidence, or H6 fresh-evaluator handoff. The GitNexus index and generated agent context are refreshed against commit f8a6e0e7 with 23,440 symbols, 34,647 relationships, and 300 execution flows.

blockers.title: Live provider credentials are unavailable for H5 paired routing evidence.
A foreign canonical MCP runtime with a mismatched lock digest cannot be adopted without verified ownership.

risks.title: Cursor CLI is unavailable locally and Antigravity lacks a live first-party hook validator; these adapters currently rely on native-schema review plus deterministic shell and payload canaries.
risks.mitigation: Keep both adapters fail-open and in observe mode, preserve their static contract tests, and run a live host canary before enabling any stronger behavior.

next_actions.title: Implement the H2 TrajectoryLedger, cancellation/disposer semantics, and quiescence receipts.
